## Body

Security verdict, #315 at 916de56 (F258 live index, migration 0049, R312-N1). Read-only review of the diff; nothing built, the live DB untouched.

Bound parameters: PASS. LIST_LIVE_SQL is a static &str. `list` chooses one of three constants and binds the same five parameters (?1 harness, ?2 folder, ?3 parent, ?4 pane, ?5 live_only as i64). No string building. The migration is DDL plus `PRAGMA user_version = 49`, with no data, paths, ids or secrets. A grep of the full diff for /Users/, token, secret, key and password markers found nothing. The tests and docs carry only row counts and timings. Safe to publish.

Row-set equivalence (which seats the sweep and the other live_only callers see): PASS. LIST_LIVE_SQL equals LIST_SQL with ?5 = 1: the same four guard predicates, `tombstoned_at IS NULL`, and ORDER BY id. On this branch `?5 <> 0` is always true, because it is taken only when live_only is set. SQLite maintains the partial index's membership on every insert, update and delete, so a live row cannot be missing from seats_live. Every other live_only caller sees the same rows as before: identity/whoami, directory, routes, delivery, registration, the binds, cache_proxy and the pane observer.

Reaper: behaviour-preserving, and it cannot act on a tombstoned seat or revive one. The old code already dropped tombstoned rows in Rust before the loop, so the candidate set is unchanged. The loop still re-reads each row with `registry.get` and skips it if `tombstoned_at` is set. It still re-checks eligibility, and `tombstone_if_unchanged` (a CAS) remains the authority. A row tombstoned or re-incarnated between the list and the act gives `incarnation-changed`, exactly as before. No path writes tombstoned_at = NULL, and the sweep never needs a tombstoned row (re-tombstone, receipt or revive). A dead live seat can't be missed: it is in the live list by construction.

Fail mode when the index is missing: it fails closed. INDEXED BY refuses, `list` returns Err, the sweep returns Err for that tick, and identity lookups error rather than widen. The index is present on every v49 store. An older binary on a v49 store refuses at require_current_schema (found 49 > expected 48, "upgrade pij"), which is also closed.

Note for performance and the reviewer (cost, not security): the death sweep calls `reap_with_reason` with dry_run = false, and on that path `receipt.after` (reaper.rs, after the loop) still runs `registry.list(SeatFilter::default())`. That is the full LIST_SQL materialisation of all ~3,262 rows, filtered in Rust, every 5 s. So the "reaper list 6.26 -> 0.34 ms" claim holds for the first list only, and each sweep still pays one full roster scan. The fix is a live_only list (`.len()`). Not blocking on security.
